title: Ancient climate records reveal how East Asian monsoon shifted abruptly into cold and drought
summary: How does climate change affect the East Asian monsoon? Researchers from Utrecht University's Faculty of Geosciences, together with colleagues at research institutes in China and Belgium, are investigating this question by looking back 250,000 years. They found that, over long timescales, the monsoon system tracks changes in incoming solar radiation caused by variations in Earth's orbit and tilt. But when radiation falls below a certain threshold, abrupt periods of extreme cold and drought occur, particularly when atmospheric CO₂ concentrations are low. The study was published in Communications Earth & Environment.

title: A new view of the gamma-ray gap: 14 years of Fermi data reveal around 450 sources in a largely unexplored energy range
summary: The universe is filled with light at many different energies. Some of it is invisible to our eyes, including extremely energetic gamma rays, which can only be produced in the most extreme environments in our universe, for example supermassive black holes, exploding stars or astrophysical jets. To "see" gamma rays, astrophysicists use particle experiments in space, such as the Fermi-Large Area Telescope (Fermi-LAT). This instrument was launched into space by NASA in 2008, and it can detect photons from 20 megaelectronvolts (MeV, a unit of energy) to beyond 1 teraelectronvolt (TeV).
